items.headline: Lead: Thursday is tomorrow, and the new quarterback is not for Thursday
paragraphs: There are no NFL games today, Wednesday, November 4. The next game is Jacksonville at Baltimore on Thursday, November 5, at 8:15 p.m. ET.

The big Wednesday news does not change Thursday's starter. Baltimore is finalizing a trade with Arizona for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, but the deal is not expected to be completed until the weekend, so Brissett would debut the following Monday, November 16, against the Los Angeles Chargers. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano still starts Thursday night against Jacksonville, his first career start.

Do not let the trade headline move your Thursday read. Thursday's quarterback is Fagnano. The inactive list lands about 90 minutes before kickoff Thursday, and that is the last check before you act on a Thursday price.
items.takeaway: Thursday is Jacksonville at Baltimore at 8:15 p.m. ET; Fagnano still starts, and Brissett is a next-week story, not a Thursday one.

items.headline: Injury roundup: final designations are in — Tuten and Walker questionable, Wiggins questionable, Ioane clear
paragraphs: Baltimore's quarterback room is now settled for Thursday and thin behind it. Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve after right thumb surgery, and Tyler Huntley is out for the season after further testing showed a season-ending turf toe injury that will require surgery. Fagnano, who was a full participant Tuesday with his ankle heavily taped, starts. Kedon Slovis and Austin Reed back him up.

Elsewhere for Baltimore, rookie guard Vega Ioane carries no designation on Wednesday's final injury report and is set to return after missing one game with a knee injury. Cornerback Nate Wiggins missed Wednesday's practice with an illness and is questionable for Thursday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins will miss a third straight game with a knee injury. Kicker Tyler Loop is on injured reserve with a groin injury, so Jake Moody is expected to kick Thursday.

For Jacksonville, running back Bhayshul Tuten is questionable and a game-time decision, according to head coach Liam Coen. Tuten did not practice all week with ankle and foot injuries. Defensive end Travon Walker is questionable with a rib injury after limited practices Tuesday and Wednesday. Wide receiver Jakobi Meyers, running back Chris Rodriguez Jr., guard Ezra Cleveland, and safety Antonio Johnson carry no game status and are good to go. Defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton and safety Eric Murray are out for the season.
items.takeaway: Fagnano starts with Huntley out for the season; Tuten and Walker are game-time questions, Ioane is clear, and Wiggins is questionable with an illness.

items.headline: Weather: rain chances rise through Thursday evening in Baltimore, wind light
paragraphs: Thursday night in Baltimore looks mild with rain in the picture. The forecast for M&T Bank Stadium calls for temperatures in the high 60s at kickoff, falling into the mid-60s through the evening, with a chance of rain showers that rises as the night goes on. Wind is light, out of the south at just a few miles per hour around kickoff.

That is a factual weather read, not a totals edge. Mostly dry conditions are expected around the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, with an isolated shower or thunderstorm possible during the game. If you are going, pack for rain. If you are betting, do not turn a rain chance into a totals opinion on its own.
items.takeaway: Thursday night in Baltimore: high 60s at kickoff, light south wind, and a rising chance of rain showers through the evening.

So there are no Thursday cards to read tonight: no Hit Rate, Balanced, or Value pick for Jacksonville at Baltimore on the board yet. The only cards on it are Monday's history, covered this morning. Do not force a pick out of a stale board.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Learn the Game: what handle and tickets tell you — and what they do not
paragraphs: Two numbers show up on every betting-splits page, and they are not the same thing. Tickets, sometimes labeled BET, are the share of individual bets on a side. Handle, labeled HND, is the share of money on a side.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say a team gets 70% of the tickets but only 40% of the handle. That means lots of small bets are on that team, while fewer, larger bets are on the other side. It does not prove sharper bettors are on the other side, and it does not prove the line will move that way.

A real split worth watching needs a disagreement plus something else — a line move in the same direction, or a second book showing the same pattern. Tickets and handle agreeing on the same side is not a fade signal. It is just a popular side.
items.takeaway: Tickets count bets, handle counts money; a gap between them is a question to check against line movement, not a pick on its own.

items.headline: Thursday's line has settled around Jacksonville by 10, and the total sits near 40
paragraphs: This is all one move, and it is still the quarterback story. The shadow-tracked lookahead had Baltimore as a 3-point favorite with a total of 48.5. It reopened after Week 8 with Jacksonville favored by 7.5, then climbed to Jacksonville -9.5 with the total down to 40.5 by Tuesday evening.

This morning it stretched a little further, to Jacksonville -9.5 at one book and Baltimore +10 at another, with the total at 40 to 40.5. This evening the consensus sits in the same place: Jacksonville -9.5 to -10, with the total at 39.5 to 40.5 and the moneyline around Jacksonville -470 to -525 and Baltimore +360 to +390. The big move is over; the last day has been small ticks around 10 and 40, not a new direction.

The app has not caught this move yet — its board still shows Week 8, generated November 2, with no Week 9 cards at all, and its Week 8 Baltimore game does not even list a starting quarterback. So do not look to the board for Thursday's price. If your book has a Thursday line, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.

items.headline: Thursday game? Thursday check.
paragraphs: The quarterback question is answered and the trade news does not change Thursday, so there is no reason to wait on that news anymore. If your book has a Thursday number you like, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. A good number today beats a hoped-for number later, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.

The one thing still worth waiting on is the inactive list, about 90 minutes before kickoff Thursday. If Tuten, Walker, or Wiggins changes status there, run your price through Check again before you act.

Odds are price mechanics: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and staking setting — that part is deliberately conservative, and it lives in the app, not here. Settlement in the tracker is manual, and it only works if you are honest with yourself — log the losers too.
items.takeaway: Thursday game? Thursday check. Run your book's Thursday price through Check now, and re-check if the inactive list changes anything.
